subtopics.title: The Scale from Impossible to Certain

questions.question: The probability scale runs from:
options: 0 for impossible to 1 for certain, with nothing beyond either end

questions.question: A spinner with eight equal sectors, one marked WIN, gives a winning probability of:
An 'event' differs from an 'outcome' because an event:
options: Is the collection of outcomes you care about — 'even' bundles 2, 4 and 6

questions.question: If the spinner wins with probability one eighth, it loses with probability:
options: Seven eighths — the two must total exactly 1

questions.question: The taxi arrived full on 12 of 40 mornings. The relative frequency of a full taxi is:
Taxis, weather and load shedding need relative frequency rather than theoretical probability because:
options: They have no symmetry to consult — their chances must be estimated by watching
Theoretical probability only works for large numbers

questions.question: Seven heads in ten tosses of a fair coin means:
options: The theoretical probability has changed to 0,7
Nothing alarming — small samples wobble; a thousand tosses at that rate would be evidence
The next three tosses must be tails

questions.question: A coin tossed 200 times gives 92 heads. The full-marks comparison says:
options: The coin is unfair because 92 is not 100
Theoretical 0,5, relative frequency 0,46 — close together, so the coin behaves fairly over a decent test

subtopics.title: Tree Diagrams: Chance in Two Steps

questions.question: Tossing a coin twice produces the equally likely combined outcomes:
options: Heads-heads, heads-tails, tails-heads, tails-tails — four routes
Two heads or two tails only

questions.question: The probability of exactly one head in two tosses is:
options: A half — the two routes heads-tails and tails-heads

questions.question: The rule for combining probabilities along a tree's branches is:
options: Subtract the smaller from the larger
Multiply along the route — a half times a half gives each coin path a quarter

questions.question: If the tuck shop runs out of pies with probability 0,2 each day, independently, then pies available two days running has probability:

subtopics.title: Two-Way Tables: Chance in a Grid

questions.question: With 28 learner-taxi, 42 learner-foot, 20 adult-taxi and 30 adult-foot, the totals are:
options: 70 learners, 50 adults, 48 by taxi, 72 on foot, 120 in all
60 learners, 60 adults, 50 by taxi, 70 on foot
70 learners, 50 adults, 50 by taxi, 70 on foot
48 learners, 72 adults, 70 by taxi, 50 on foot

questions.question: The probability that a random visitor is an adult who came by taxi is:
options: The single cell 20 over the grand total 120 — one sixth

questions.question: 'Given that a visitor is a learner, the chance they came by taxi' is:
options: 28 over 70 = 0,4 — the words shrink the world to the 70 learners

questions.question: Choosing the denominator in a two-way-table question depends on:
options: The wording — grand total for 'a random visitor', a row or column total when the question says 'given' or 'of the learners'

questions.question: One half, 0,5 and 50% are:
options: The same chance in three languages — fraction, decimal and percent
Increasingly likely versions of the same event

questions.question: Picking a red sweet blind from a packet of 3 red and 9 green has probability:
An answer of 1,2 for a probability is:
options: Acceptable if the working is shown
Broken — nothing is more certain than certain, so no probability exceeds 1

subtopics.title: The Taxi You Watched for Forty Mornings

questions.question: The taxi's chance had to be watched rather than calculated because:
options: There is no rulebook of symmetry for taxis — real-world chances are measured by counting
The counting was easier than the formula
Coins are more reliable than timetables

questions.question: Forty mornings of watching beats four mornings because:
options: The longer you watch, the closer the count creeps to the truth
Four mornings would give probability zero
The taxi changes route after four days

questions.question: Nomsa's estimate of 0,3 for a full taxi means roughly:
options: The taxi is full every third week
Three taxis in ten are full right now
A thirty percent risk of standing at a full taxi's door on any school morning

subtopics.title: Branches and Grids: Handling Two Things at Once

questions.question: The tree diagram exists mainly to:
options: Put every path in front of your eyes, catching the route head-counters forget — like tails-heads

questions.question: The picture for a crowd where each person carries two labels is:
options: The two-way grid, with cells and totals that must add up

questions.question: When rows and columns of the grid refuse to add to their totals:
options: The grand total should be changed
A cell is wrong, and finding it before answering is free

questions.question: Seeing 'given that' or 'of the learners' in a question means:
options: Add the row and column totals
The denominator stops being 120 and becomes the named group's total
